name: Track Order History for WooCommerce
author: AddWeb Solution

sections.description:
When you look at an order, you want to know who you are dealing with: is this a new customer or a regular? Do they often cancel? What do they usually buy? Track Order History for WooCommerce shows this right where you work, and gives your customers a clear overview of their own orders in My Account.

For shop managers (WooCommerce > Orders)

  • Past orders column on the Orders list, with a New or Returning label.
  • Customer badges for returning customers, with your own rules: by total spent, by number of orders, or both combined (AND / OR). Make tiers such as Gold, Silver and Bronze (up to 10); the first badge that matches is shown. Loyal (5 orders) is ready to use; VIP is ready once you set an amount.
  • 13 ready-made badge designs: Gold, Silver, Bronze and Platinum medals, VIP crown, Diamond, Heart, Star, Rising, Trophy, and Warning shield, Warning sign and Stop sign for risk. Or upload your own badge image from the Media Library.
  • Risk warning: a badge when a customer has too many problem orders: by number, by share of all orders (for example 30%), or both. You choose which statuses count (cancelled, failed, refunded), so you can check before you ship.
  • Order history pop-up on every order: click the number to see all orders of the customer (this order included and marked, also for first-time customers and guests) with date, status, products (product ID, name and quantity) and total, plus total orders, total spent, net spent after refunds, average order and “customer since”.
  • Most bought products and buying rhythm: “orders about every 25 days, last order 40 days ago”, with an Overdue label for regulars who stopped buying.
  • Customer notes: a private staff note (“Always call before delivery”) shown on every order of that customer, also for guests.
  • Order history box on the order screen, with the summary, the latest orders and the note editor.
  • Guest customers included: guest orders are matched by billing email, also guest orders a customer placed before registering.
  • View all orders of this customer: one click to the Orders list filtered to that customer.
  • Orders and Total spent columns in Users > All Users.

For customers (My Account)

  • Order summary on the dashboard: number of orders, total spent, average order, last order and the latest orders.
  • Date filters: Today, Last 30 days, Last 12 months, All time, or any year and month. The same filters work on the Orders page.
  • Buy again: one click puts the products of a past order back in the cart, next to what is already there. Out-of-stock products are skipped.
  • Your favourites: the products the customer buys most, with an Add to cart button.

On any page: one shortcode

  • [wptoh_orders] shows the customer’s order summary, orders (table or cards, with products and Buy again), last order, favourites or a single figure, on any page.
  • A visual shortcode builder in WooCommerce > Order History > Shortcode: pick the options, see a live preview as a real customer, and copy the shortcode.
  • Works in the block editor and in the shortcode element of every page builder: Elementor, Bricks, Divi, WPBakery and others.

Customers only ever see their own orders. Notes, risk warnings and labels are never shown to customers.

Built on WooCommerce

  • Works with High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) and with the classic order storage.
  • Uses WooCommerce’s own order functions, My Account hooks and reorder feature, so it works with any theme.
  • Fast: cached figures and count queries, and only the orders that are shown are loaded.
  • Every feature can be turned on or off in WooCommerce > Order History, a modern settings page with tabs, switches and a live badge preview.
  • Custom CSS for the shop pages: restyle the customer order summary, filters and favourites from the settings, with WordPress’s code editor.
  • A clean, modern indigo design for all order screens and the pop-up.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from Plugins > Add New, or upload the wc-past-orders folder to /wp-content/plugins/. WooCommerce must be active.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open WooCommerce > Orders: the “Past orders” column is next to the Total column.
  4. Optional: adjust the labels, the risk warning and the My Account features in WooCommerce > Order History.
sections.faq:
Does it work with High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS)?

Yes. It works with HPOS on or off, using WooCommerce’s own order functions. With HPOS, use WooCommerce 8.2 or later (the version in which HPOS became stable); with the classic order storage, WooCommerce 7.0 or later.

How are guest customers handled?

Guest orders are matched by billing email. A registered customer’s history also includes guest orders placed with the email address of their account, and a guest order placed with a registered customer’s account email shows that customer’s history. Emails typed at checkout are not verified, so treat the matching as a helpful guide.

Which orders count towards “Total spent”?

Paid orders (processing and completed), before refunds, as in WooCommerce’s own customer figures. When a customer has refunds, the pop-up also shows “Net spent” after refunds.

Why can the Users list show a lower total than the history?

The Orders and Total spent columns in Users > All Users show WooCommerce’s own figures for the customer account. The order history also includes guest orders placed with the same email address.

What do customers see?

On the My Account dashboard: their order summary with date filters, their latest orders with a “Buy again” button, and their favourite products. The Orders page gets the same date filters and a “Buy again” button. Customers only see the orders of their own account; staff notes, risk warnings and VIP labels are never shown to them. Each feature can be turned off in WooCommerce > Order History.

How do I show a customer’s orders on my own page or in a page builder?

Use the shortcode [wptoh_orders]. The easiest way is the Shortcode tab in WooCommerce > Order History: choose what to show, check the live preview and copy the shortcode. Paste it into a Shortcode block, or the shortcode element of Elementor, Bricks, Divi (Code or Text module) or WPBakery (Text block). Main options: show (summary, orders, last_order, favourites, stat), range, filters, limit, layout (table or cards), products, buy_again, stat, guest (login, message or hide). Visitors who are not logged in see a login button by default.

Can I switch off everything customers see?

Yes. WooCommerce > Order History has a master switch on the My Account tab (hides the summary, date filters, Buy again and favourites) and one on the Shortcode tab (every [wptoh_orders] on the site shows nothing, without editing the pages). Your other choices are kept for when you switch them back on. The admin features are not affected.

Can I change how the My Account pages look?

Yes. In WooCommerce > Order History > My Account, add your own CSS in the Custom CSS box (administrators, or anyone who may edit CSS). It loads on the My Account pages after the plugin’s styles. The help text lists the class names to use.

Does “Buy again” empty the cart?

No. It adds the products of the order to what is already in the cart, using WooCommerce’s add to cart: quantities add up, and products that are out of stock or no longer available are skipped, with a message.

How do customer badges work?

In WooCommerce > Order History > Customer badges, each badge has a rule: total spent, number of orders, both (AND) or either (OR). Badges are checked from top to bottom and the first one that matches is shown, so put your highest tier first. Only returning customers (2 or more orders) get a badge. Use the arrows to change the order, and “Add badge” for more tiers (up to 10).

Can I use my own badge image?

Yes. Each badge (and the risk badge) can use one of the 13 ready-made badge designs, or an image you upload or choose from the Media Library. A small square PNG, JPG or WebP works best.

How is the risk warning counted?

You choose which statuses are problem orders (cancelled, failed, refunded) and the rule: a number of problem orders (2 by default), a share of all the customer’s orders (judged from 3 orders on), or both. The badge shows the number of problem orders; the pop-up always shows the details.

Where are customer notes stored? Are they personal data?

Notes of registered customers are stored in their user profile, notes of guests in one plugin option. Notes are never shown in the shop, but they are personal data: they are included in WordPress’s personal data export and erase tools (Tools > Export / Erase Personal Data), so write them as you would write anything the customer may one day read. A suggested privacy policy text is added under Settings > Privacy. Notes are removed when you delete the plugin.

Who can see the order history?

Users who can manage WooCommerce orders (shop managers and administrators). The history is only loaded for them.

Does the plugin store any data?

It reads WooCommerce’s orders and never changes them. It stores its settings, customer notes and cached figures (which expire after a day). No tables are added. Everything is removed when you delete the plugin.
sections.changelog:
2.2.0

  • New: One shortcode, [wptoh_orders], shows the customer’s orders on any page or page builder: summary, orders (table or cards, with products and Buy again), last order, favourites or a single figure.
  • New: Visual shortcode builder with live preview and copy button (WooCommerce > Order History > Shortcode).
  • New: Options for visitors who are not logged in: login button (back to the page), message or nothing.
  • New: Master switches: turn off everything in My Account, or every [wptoh_orders] shortcode on the site, with one click. Your other choices are kept.
  • Fix: “Buy again” now adds to the quantity already in the cart. Before, a product already in the cart got the order’s quantity instead, and a wrong “unavailable” message could appear.
  • Fix: The orders table looks right and stacks on phones in block themes such as Twenty Twenty-Five, not only in classic WooCommerce themes.

2.1.0

  • New: Customer badges with rules by total spent, number of orders, or both (AND / OR); up to 10 tiers, first match wins.
  • New: 13 ready-made badge designs (medals, crown, diamond, heart, star, rising, trophy, and three risk signs), or your own image from the Media Library.
  • New: Custom CSS box for the My Account pages (users who may edit CSS).
  • New: Modern indigo design for the Orders column, pop-up, order screen box and settings page.
  • New: Order screens options: show or hide customer badges, the risk badge and the note marker in the Orders list, and the Products column in the pop-up.
  • New: Risk warning by number or share of problem orders; choose which statuses count.
  • New: Customer notes: a private staff note shown on every order of that customer (also guests), with privacy export and erase.
  • New: The order history pop-up opens from every order (also first orders and guests) and lists all orders of the customer, this order included, with products (product ID, name, quantity).
  • New: Most bought products and buying rhythm (average days between orders, last order, Overdue label) in the pop-up and on the order screen.
  • New: Net spent after refunds.
  • New: My Account order summary with date filters (Today, Last 30 days, Last 12 months, All time, year and month).
  • New: The same date filters on the My Account Orders page.
  • New: “Buy again” button on past orders (adds to the cart, skips out-of-stock products).
  • New: “Your favourites” on the My Account dashboard.
  • New: Settings page with tabs and a live badge preview: WooCommerce > Order History.
  • Change: The order screen box is now called “Order history” (WooCommerce has its own “Customer history” box).
  • Compatibility: Tested with WordPress 7.2 and WooCommerce 7.0 to 11.3, with HPOS on and off.

2.0.0

  • New: Order history pop-up with date, status and total of each order, plus total orders, total spent, average order and “customer since”.
  • New: “Customer history” box on the order screen.
  • New: Guest customers: orders are matched by billing email (also guest orders of registered customers).
  • New: New / Returning customer label in the Past orders column.
  • New: “View all orders of this customer” link.
  • New: Orders and Total spent columns in Users > All Users.
  • Security: The order history request now requires a logged-in shop manager or administrator and a security token. Before, anyone could request a customer’s order numbers.
  • Compatibility: Works with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) and declares compatibility; the column now also appears on the HPOS orders screen.
  • Improvement: Much faster orders list: uses WooCommerce’s cached customer totals instead of loading every order of every customer.
  • Improvement: Accessible pop-up (keyboard, Escape to close, focus handling); no jQuery.
  • Improvement: Script and styles load only on the WooCommerce order screens.
  • Fix: PHP 8.2 deprecation notice on every request.
  • Fix: The plugin no longer deactivates itself when WooCommerce is unavailable; it shows a notice instead.
  • Compatibility: Tested with WordPress 7.2 and WooCommerce 7.0 to 11.3. Requires WordPress 6.5, PHP 7.4 and WooCommerce 7.0 or later.

1.4

  • Updated plugin for compatibility with the latest WordPress version.

1.3

  • Compatibility check with WordPress 6.3.

1.2

  • Updated author details.

1.1

  • Added admin notice if WooCommerce is not activated.

1.0.0

  • First release.
